svg.text: Everyday English - Quote
Clarity begins when we
name what matters.
MEANING
Identifying a priority can make a confusing situation
easier to understand.
IN CONTEXT
With three deadlines competing for attention, Jo
reminded herself, “Clarity begins when we name
what matters.” She chose the most important task.
USAGE NOTE
Name here means identify or state explicitly, rather
than give someone a name. Use the sentence when
discussing priorities or clarifying what is most
important.
CONVERSATION
A: Everything feels urgent. Where do I start?
B: “Clarity begins when we name what matters.”
Which deadline affects someone else?
A: The application. My colleague needs it today.
B: Then make that your first priority.
YOUR TURN
Use the quote to introduce one priority and explain
why it matters. Model: Finishing the application
matters because someone is waiting for it.
